Thrive

THRYVE — rhymes with 'alive'; to thrive is to be more than just alive, but truly flourishing. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To thrive is to grow, develop, or do well vigorously and successfully.

Despite the rocky soil, the old olive trees continued to thrive for centuries.

Worked Example

A small coffee shop opens on a quiet side street with almost no customers. Within two years, lines form out the door every morning, and the owner opens two more locations across town.

Growing from almost nothing into clear, vigorous success is exactly what it means to thrive. Unlike 'survive,' which just means barely making it through, thriving means flourishing and growing stronger.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

flourish: to grow or develop in a healthy, vigorous way

prosper: to succeed and do well, especially financially

blossom: to develop in a promising, healthy way

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

wither: to become weak, shriveled, or lose vitality

languish: to lose strength or fail to progress

Where it sits · how vigorously it grows — survive → thrive → boom

survive vs. thrive: To survive is weaker than to thrive — surviving just means barely making it through, while thriving means actually growing strong and successful.

boom vs. thrive: To boom is stronger than to thrive in a sense: thriving is steady, healthy growth, but a boom is a sudden, dramatic surge of growth all at once.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — thrive-

root — thrive-: to grasp, seize (later: to prosper) (Old Norse)

Put it together

Put it together: Thrive comes from Old Norse thrifa, meaning 'to grasp or seize.' Over time the sense shifted from grabbing hold of something to flourishing and growing strong, as if grasping onto success.

Use the root in a new word: thriving

Use the root in a new word: thriving: The thriving little bakery outgrew its original storefront within a year.
